sampling_model.design: Conditional on each fixed covariate stratum, \(Z\) is randomized with known \(\pi_z(x)=P(Z=z\mid X=x)\) and \(\min_{x,z}\{P(X=x),\pi_z(x)\}\ge\pi_*\); the observed count vector satisfies \(N_n\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}\{n,p_n(u)\}\).
sampling_model.units: The categorical support \(\mathcal J\), rational wage grid \(\mathcal Y\), rational quantile grid \(\mathcal T\), and assertion list \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\) are fixed while \(n\to\infty\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument \(Z\), received treatment \(D\), and selection indicator \(S\) are binary; wages are observed only when \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Positive multinomial cells, randomized-instrument support, and target-mass positivity remain distinct conditions. Causal tangent legality additionally requires \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\); both are certified from rational response-type face data.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On every fixed compact, base convergence and the centered local expansion imply eventual positive cells and lawful causal parameters. Carter then contributes only the bounded-ratio experiment error; the score mean, covariance, active-face remainder, rational offset, and semantic-union displacement are charged separately. The diagonal radius records exactly where all such compact moduli have passed, and no premise constrains a label boundary inserted beyond that radius.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.4 proves that recession cones form a rational fan under connectedness and the Minkowski--Weyl condition.
Theorems 3.32 and 4.8 construct a compatible compactified polyhedral complex and compute its Hasse diagram combinatorially.
Corollary 4 gives an explicit smoothing, truncation, and discretization error for Gaussian integration over a polytope.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a near-optimal affine detector for two compact convex composite hypotheses through a convex-concave saddle point.
Theorems 1--3 prove convergence of finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations to compact-parameter minimax expected-size confidence regions.
Theorem 1.3 gives a randomized \(O^*(n^3)\) relative-error algorithm for Gaussian volume of a convex set containing the unit ball in the membership-oracle model.
The paper gives convergence conditions for adaptive discretization of finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs with unbounded variables.
Theorem 1 bounds the Le Cam distance between a multinomial experiment and a matching Gaussian experiment when cell-probability ratios are bounded.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniform coverage for calibrated projection under drifting moment inequalities, and Theorem 3.2 gives an optimization convergence rate on a compact rectangle.
The paper derives sharp marginal quantile-treatment-effect bounds under truncation by death.
Propositions 1--2 derive nonparametric bounds for average wage effects among always-employed compliers in Job Corps.

Under the complier-conditional weak-selection condition in Assumption 3.2, Proposition 3.1 gives sharp mean SLATE bounds for always-selected compliers, and Theorem 4.1 gives inference and joint asymptotic normality.

Theorem 1 proves minimum average Lebesgue volume for the inverted minimal-cardinality multinomial covering collections of Definition 1, and Proposition 1 selects a maximum-coverage tie-break among those minimizers.

Section 5 and Proposition 1 present sharp quantile-treatment-effect bounds for the always-employed stratum under random assignment and individual-level employment monotonicity, and Section 6.4 evaluates those bounds at multiple Job Corps wage quantiles.

body.tldr: The Carter comparison spine is now explicit and proves fixed-compact and compatible moving-offset multinomial transfer with separate score, covariance, boundary, and semantic-geometry charges. An explicit escaping-boundary array falsifies the global upper minimax implication under compact-uniform assumptions; the corrected result is a global liminf plus two-sided convergence on a diagonal expanding lawful window. The causal same-law endpoint conclusions and conditional Gaussian certificate remain intact. Effective compatible density remains open: common-ray Følner factors yield path-independent incidence operators and an explicit boundary ratio, but not the required face-to-cone Gaussian-weighted equality and uniform separated-risk preservation.

project_justification.gap: Carter's bounded-ratio theorem gives parameter-independent kernels for a fixed multinomial experiment and its matched Gaussian experiment, but it does not compare moving causal truth regions or control parameters escaping every compact. Existing recession geometry likewise does not prove that incident statistical chart rules have vanishing Gaussian-weighted discrepancy.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification assertions combine discontinuous completed labels, intersecting unbounded recession faces, and a global honesty constraint. Compact local asymptotics can coexist with an entirely new hard label seam at an escaping parameter, so local experiment comparison and global minimax transfer are mathematically distinct problems.
project_justification.fill: The proved layer now contains Carter's exact positive-cell specialization, bounded-loss total-variation propagation, computable finite-arrangement stability, fixed-compact and moving-offset transfer, a global certificate-first liminf, and two-sided expanding-window convergence. A common-ray Følner construction also supplies coherent incidence transitions and explicit translation boundary ratios; the unresolved contribution is the simultaneous face-to-cone density theorem needed for unconditional global CertGluePFL certification.

body.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) is now invoked at its exact scope: bounded-ratio multinomial laws versus matched multivariate normal laws through parameter-independent kernels, with error proportional to the fixed cell count times its logarithm over square-root sample size. The present transfer adds the fixed score map, covariance replacement, completed-affine-arrangement stability, and moving-offset boundary ledger. Carter does not supply any of those semantic steps or unbounded-domain uniformity. Polyhedral compactification and Gaussian-integration references remain informative ingredients rather than a solution to simultaneous recession compatibility.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The common-ray operators commute and have explicit Følner boundary ratios, but adding cone-only ray factors can still change an arbitrary face rule by order one; simultaneous Gaussian-weighted face compatibility and separated-risk preservation therefore remain open. The compact-uniform transfer assumptions are also insufficient for a global upper minimax bound, as shown by the escaping-boundary witness. What is proved is fixed-compact transfer, compatible moving-offset transfer on compacts, a global liminf from finite dual certificates, and two-sided convergence for the diagonal expanding-window functional. The milliscale four-label certificate remains open.
body.honest_scope: The causal estimand is still the same-law joint identified set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp endpoint intervals. Carter-backed sampled-data claims are compact or expanding-window claims. The original global multinomial value has a proved lower limit but no proved upper limit under the current hypotheses, and no globally honest unbounded transferred primal is claimed. Gaussian CertGluePFL output remains conditional on effective compatible density, whose exact unresolved step is the simultaneous face-to-cone weighted approximation.
body.interpretation: The Gaussian experiment remains the correct local decision target on every fixed lawful direction window. Its minimax value is also the limit of the explicitly defined expanding-window multinomial values and a lower limit for the original global values. It is not identified as the two-sided limit of the global unbounded multinomial problem: compact local expansions permit statistically hard assertion boundaries to escape to infinity.
